messages:
maya: FYI — ran into a bundler + edge runtime bug when using a symlinked local package in a monorepo (vite/rollup/webpack all affected). Minimal repro below, hoping someone can triage.

maya: Repro steps (very small):
1) repo root with `app/` and `packages/ui-lib/` where ui-lib is npm-linked or `pnpm-workspace` symlink.
2) `ui-lib` publishes ESM-only exports ("type": "module") and uses an index.js that re-exports default from ./dist/index.mjs
3) app imports: `import Button from 'ui-lib'` and runs on the edge runtime with our SDK edge-bundle.

maya: Commands I ran:
```
# from repo root
cd app
pnpm install --shamefully-hoist # reproduces with pnpm and with plain npm link
pnpm build
pnpm start:edge
```

maya: Error seen in edge logs: `TypeError: require is not defined` - but stack shows it originated from a resolved vendor chunk that contains a transpiled CJS wrapper for ui-lib, even though ui-lib is ESM.

simon: :eyes: do you have the chunk file or stack trace? that sounds like a resolver picked the wrong entry.

maya: stack snippet:
```
Error: Uncaught TypeError: require is not defined
 at file:///workspace/.cache/vite/deps/vendor-ui-lib.js:12:15
 at async init (file:///workspace/.cache/vite/entry-server.js:45:7)
```

maya: package.json from ui-lib:
```
{
  "name": "ui-lib",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "default": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

alex: ah — default export points to a cjs file which bundlers sometimes prefer for `require` interop during dedupe. if the resolver ends up rewriting to the cjs path for the symlinked package, edge runtime fails.

tyler: does this only happen for symlinked deps? or also for normal installed deps?

maya: normal installed deps (from registry) work fine. this only triggers when the package is a symlinked local package. I suspect resolver heuristics in the bundlers treat file: or workspace packages differently and fall back to default export.

simon: can you try forcing the bundler to prefer `import` condition on the package? for vite/rollup there's `browserFields`/`mainFields` style options, and `resolve.mainFields: ['module','main']` in webpack.

maya: tried `resolve.mainFields = ['module','main']` in webpack and `optimizeDeps: { esbuildOptions: { mainFields: ['module','browser'] }}` for vite — no luck. The symlinked path still resolves to the cjs file.

alex: hmm. can you share the reproduction repo? even a tiny one. if not public, w/ an archive.

maya: uploaded a tiny repro to our internal gist: https://internal.redwood/repros/symlink-bundler-edge-2951234567.tar.gz

ci-bot: build: CI job #4821 started for branch maya/symlink-bundler-repro (quick heads up).

tyler: temporary workaround for folks hitting this: ensure ui-lib's exports only include ESM entry (remove the default cjs fallback) or set package.json `exports: {"import":"./dist/index.mjs"}`. Not ideal but helps unblock.

simon: longer term fix ideas: 1) update our edge bundling plugin to prefer `exports.import` unconditionally for local file: or workspace packages; 2) detect a symlinked package and emit a warning suggesting removing cjs fallback; 3) add a small transform in the edge runtime to error earlier with a clearer message.

alex: agree. PR sketch: `plugins/resolve-workspace.js` that detects link/symlink and injects a virtual resolution map to force ESM entry. low risk.

maya: I'll put together a tiny PR with tests for vite + webpack + rollup and link the repro. will ping here when ready.

simon: thanks — also add a note in the onboarding docs for monorepos: "avoid cjs fallback for workspace packages when targeting edge runtimes". good quick doc link prevents future confusion.

maya: done — created draft PR and a docs blurb (internal): https://go/repo/pr/4201. tag me for reviews.

alex: :thumbsup: thanks — this matches a support ticket we saw last week from a customer using pnpm workspace. good catch.

maya: any preferred test harness? I used `node --conditions=import` + `vite build --ssr` locally. open to suggestions for CI steps.

tyler: add matrix for bundlers in CI job: vite/rollup/webpack + symlink vs published. that should catch regressions.

maya: will do. last note: reproducer only repros in edge-like runtime (no global require shim). Regular node mode works because CJS interop layer provides `require`. hence hard to catch in typical unit tests.

simon: perfect — thanks for filing. leaving reaction.

maya: thanks all.
